messages:
olivia: quick heads up — while validating partner onboarding artifacts I found a KMS-wrapped blob inside an archive in partner-ci-uploads. the object path: s3://partner-onboard/archives/2026-03-21/artifact.tar.gz. looks like a wrapped service token (base64 blob). not seeing plaintext yet but we should treat as suspected credential bleed and rotate+audit. pinging sec + infra.

alex: thanks — do we know whether the blob is a GCP or AWS-wrapped ciphertext? can you paste the first 200 chars (safe redacted) or filename? also: who had access to that S3 prefix?

olivia: blob filename is artifacts/cred_blob.enc inside the tar. sample header: `kms:CiQABAs... (truncated)` — partner's onboarding script appears to have included the artifact by accident. ACLs on the prefix are: team `partner-ingest` (write), `build-bots` (read), and infra svcacct `redwood-onboard@infra` (read).

jamal: copying IAM snippet from bucket policy: `{"Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/partner-ingest"]}, "Action": ["s3:GetObject","s3:PutObject"]}`. Not wide open but partner CI and some runner images had access.

maria: we need audit logs (object access + KMS decrypt attempts) and RBAC check. please: 1) export S3 access logs for the prefix last 30d, 2) query CloudTrail/CloudAudit for any `Decrypt` on the CMK.

sec-bot: [AUTO] detection=0.82; rule=artifact-kms-ciphertext-detected; recommended_action=rotate-and-audit

olivia: filing a short incident record now. INC-2026-042 created. initial severity: P2 (suspected credential exposure w/ limited blast radius). adding folks.

alex: next steps I recommend: 1) determine whether any decrypts have occurred using the CMK's Admin audit log, 2) rotate the wrapping key (rekey) or rotate the inner credential depending on partner expectations, 3) revoke any long-lived tokens referenced by the artifact if we can identify them.

jamal: I can run a quick KMS activity query: `gcloud kms keys list --locations=global` and then `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"' --limit=50` to look for decrypt attempts. doing that now.

olivia: pulling the archive into a quarantine bucket for analysis: `aws s3 cp s3://partner-onboard/archives/2026-03-21/artifact.tar.gz s3://sec-quarantine/6324000000-artifact.tar.gz` — will not open outside secure env.

maria: on RBAC: we should temporarily restrict partner-ingest role to disallow `s3:GetObject` on that prefix until we confirm. set a scoped deny for `partner-onboard/archives/*`. I'll prepare the policy patch.

alex: also want to know if the partner used our KMS key or their own key to wrap the blob. if it's our CMK, high urgency. if it's partner-managed KMS, we notify them and ask rotation.

olivia: quick analysis: header contains `enc_type: gcp_kms_v1`, and wrapped key metadata references `projects/redwood-ops/locations/global/keyRings/onboard/cryptoKeys/onboard-wrap`. looks like our CMK used.

maria: ok that's escalated. change plan: (A) rotate/rekey our CMK (or create a new version) and rewrap any customer blobs we control, (B) force expiry / rotate any credentials that could be unwrapped by that CMK, (C) audit access and notify partner.

jamal: rekey steps — we can create a new key version and rewrap. note that automatically rewrap isn't atomic for archived objects — will need a sweep job: pseudo: ```
for obj in $(aws s3 ls s3://partner-onboard/archives/2026-03-21/ | awk '{print $4}'); do
  aws s3 cp s3://partner-onboard/archives/2026-03-21/$obj - | process-and-rewrap --kms-key=new-key; 
  aws s3 cp - s3://partner-onboard/archives/2026-03-21/$obj --metadata 'wrapped=true'
done
```

olivia: I'm ok to coordinate the sweep but prefer to keep partner’s bucket read-only and copy to sec-quarantine to rewrap there. we should also disable the old key version's `decrypt` permission while we investigate.

alex: permission delta approach: (1) create new CMK version, (2) remove decrypt binding from serviceaccounts and partner role for old key, (3) rotate inner credentials, (4) rewrap copies into quarantine with new key, (5) if all good, restore access to new-key only.

maria: I'll stage the RBAC change now. jamal — can you confirm SRE impact of removing decrypt from `redwood-onboard@infra` for 1 hour windows? we may break ongoing onboarding jobs.

jamal: short-term breakage expected for active onboarding runs. propose rolling window 1am-3am PT to minimize. will coordinate with devex.

olivia: partner notification draft: "We detected a KMS-wrapped blob included in an onboarding artifact. We have quarantined the object and initiated rotation of the wrapping key. Please rotate any credentials referenced in your artifact and confirm by EOD."

alex: also capture the object checksum and include in the ticket. good to have forensic snapshot.

olivia: checksum: sha256=9f2c... (stored in INC-2026-042).

maria: created RBAC patch draft and linked in the ticket. https://redwood-internal/runbooks/kms-rotation (runbook consulted).

sec-bot: [AUTO] checklist added to INC-2026-042: export-logs, quarantine-copy, create-key-version, revoke-old-decrypt, run-sweep, notify-partner, postmortem.

alex: who will own rotating any inner creds that belong to partner? we can rotate our CMK but we can't rotate partner secrets directly — we must request they rotate. assign outreach to bizops.

olivia: I'll ping partner-ops now and cc bizops. assigning tasks: olivia -> quarantine + partner comms; jamal -> KMS decrypt logs + sweep tooling; maria -> RBAC patch + coordinate off-window; alex -> incident lead + postmortem owner. target: rotate/widen mitigations by EOD, full sweep by EOW.

maria: noted. I'll post the RBAC temporary deny in the ticket for approval.

olivia: thanks everyone. will update INC-2026-042 as we hit milestones. :thumbsup:
